Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestInternationalFixedChronology_test_isLeapYear_loop.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestInternationalFixedChronology/TestInternationalFixedChronology_test_isLeapYear_loop.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The test's single `@Test` method only uses a handful of APIs; the dozen-plus `data_*` provider methods are never invoked. Removing that dead code and the unused imports is a pure readability win with no runtime-behavior change. Let me write the improved version.Now let me compile-check it.Compiles cleanly. I improved understandability by removing the dozen-plus unused `data_*` provider methods and the long list of now-unnecessary imports (all dead code never invoked by the single `@Test`), then named the leap-year oracle (`IS_GREGORIAN_LEAP_YEAR`), introduced `COMMON_YEAR_LENGTH`/`LEAP_YEAR_LENGTH` constants, gave variables descriptive names, and added comments explaining the Gregorian rule — all while calling the same methods with the same arguments and expected outcomes.
